body.p: This paper is in response to the Non-Final Office Action of August 8, 2024. Claims remaining in the present application are numbered 1-20. Claim 1 has been amended. No new matter has been added. The rejections and comments of the Examiner set forth in the Action have been carefully considered by the Applicant. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections and respectfully requests the Examiner to consider and allow the remaining claims.
Applicant acknowledges that claims 11-20 are in conditions for allowance.
The present Office Action rejected claims 1-10 under 35 U.S.C. §101 because the

claimed invention is directed to a judicial exception (i.e., a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea) without significantly more. To the extent the rejection still applies, this rejection is respectfully traversed in view of the following.
Cases addressing 35 U.S.C. §101 generally follow the step one(2A)/step two(2B)

Supreme Court forma under the "2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance," ("101 Guidelines") that became effective January 7, 2019. In particular, under either step 2A or 2B, Applicant respectfully asserts that the claimed invention is not directed to a judicial exception (i.e., a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea) without significantly more. In essence, guidance under the step one (Step 2A) analysis of Section 101 eligibility outlined in Alice provides that "eligibility rejections are to be applied only to claims that recite subject matter within the defined categories of judicial exceptions... [a]nd even then, a rejection would only be applied if the claim does not integrate the recited exception into a practical application." (Emphasis Added). Step two (Step 2B) of the Alice/Mayo framework is applied when step one fails to show eligibility.

Applicant cannot concur that the recited claims 1-10, as amended, fall under a judicial exception of "mental processes" under Step 2A. Specifically, the amended claims recite more than concepts performable by a human. (See page 3 of the present Action).

Under Prong One of Step 2A, Applicant respectfully asserts that the recited claims, as amended, fall outside of the judicial exception of an abstract idea as being capable of being performed in the mind because "they do not contain limitations that can practically be performed by a human mind, for instance when a human is not equipped to perform the claim limitations." (See MPEP 2106.04(a)(2) III.A. citing SRIInt'l, Inc. v. Cisco Systems, Inc., 930 F.3d 1295, 1304 (Fed. Cir. 2019). Applicant respectfully asserts that at least some claim limitations cannot be performed by human. Specifically, the amended claims recite executing on a game server game logic of a video game to generate a plurality of video frames for a game play of the video game by a player, wherein game state data is generated during the executing the game logic; identifying by the game server an effect that is generated for at least one video frame in the plurality of video frames based on the game state data; and translating by the game server the effect to a haptic response, wherein the haptic response is presented to the player simultaneous with presentation of the at least one video frame to communicate a gaming experience that is rendered by the effect in the at least one video frame. Applicant respectfully asserts that a human cannot practically perform the aforementioned operations, including the execution of game logic of a video game by a game server to generate video frames for a game play, analyzing game state data of the game play to determine an effect, translating the effect to a haptic response, and wherein the haptic response is presented to the player simultaneous with presentation of the at least one video frame. For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully asserts that the recited claims, as amended, cannot practically be performed by a human and therefore falls outside of any judicial exception.

As such, because the recited claims, as amended, fall outside of a judicial exception of an abstract idea as being capable of being performed by a human, the claims qualify as eligible subject matter, and no further analysis under Section 101 is necessary.

However, in the alternative and in furtherance of facilitating examination in accordance with the 101 Guidelines and including "The 2024 Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance Update Including on Artificial Intelligence", Applicant respectfully asserts that the recited claims, as amended, show a practical application under Step 2A, prong 2. Specifically, a
problem is identified, a solution to the problem is provided in the specification, and the claims properly reflect the technical solution.

In particular, a problem in the technology of gaming occurs when a player is unable to properly interact with a video game during game play, such that the player is gaming impaired. That is, the gaming impaired player may not be able to recognize what the video game is trying to convey, and thus is unable to perceive an intended effect during the game play. For example, a player that is hearing impaired may be unable to perceive loud sounds (i.e., the effect) generated by the video game that is intended to have the player feel a sense of urgency or ramped up intensity, which is the gaming experience that the video game is trying to convey to the player as rendered by the effect. As such, the player is unable to properly enjoy or gain the full experience when playing the video game.
An improvement to the technology is provided where computer processes are

performed on game state data to identify the effect (i.e., that is not recognized by the player) that is generated for at least one video frame during the game play, and translate that effect to a haptic response, wherein the haptic response is presented to the player simultaneous with presentation of corresponding video frames to communicate a gaming experience that is rendered by the effect. As such, the technical solution enables a gaming impaired player to properly enjoy or gain the full experience when playing a video game.
Further, a further practical solution to the technical field of gaming is provided by

identifying an effect generated by a video game with corresponding video frames, and translating the effect to a haptic response, wherein the haptic response is presented to the player simultaneous with presentation of video frames corresponding with the intended effect.
Because independent claim 1, and its dependencies, do not recite one of the

enumerated and categorized judicial exceptions and/or provide a practical application as analyzed under Prong 1 and/or Prong 2 of Step 2A, the claims go beyond the abstract idea and show eligible subject matter, and as such "then the 101 analysis is essentially concluded and the [claims are] eligible," as provided in the 101 Guidelines. No additional analysis under Section 101 is necessary.

Consequently, for at least these reasons, Applicant believes that claims 1-10, as amended, are not directed to merely abstract ideas, and as such are directed to statutory subject matter, and are allowable.
In light of the arguments presented herein, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the rejected claims for allowance thereof.

Based on the arguments presented above, Applicant respectfully asserts that pending claims 1-10 overcome the rejections of record, and/or are patentably distinct. Therefore, Applicant respectfully solicits allowance of those claims. In the present Action, claims 11-20 are allowable.
